questions.q: What inspired Bernard Sadow to put wheels on a suitcase?
a: He saw a worker roll a heavy machine through the airport
A flight attendant complained about her luggage
He read a patent for a rolling trunk
His wife suggested it on a family vacation
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he watched an airport employee wheel a big machine and realized luggage needed the same.

questions.q: How long had commercial flights existed before wheels were added to luggage?
a: Around sixty years
Around ten years
Around twenty years
Around forty years
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes people had flown for about 60 years before a luggage executive solved the obvious problem.

questions.q: Why did it take months for Sadow's wheeled suitcase to sell?
a: Buyers lacked the vision to try something new
The wheels broke during early demonstrations
Airlines refused to allow them on planes
His patent was blocked by a rival company
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the pragmatic majority resists change, so a new way takes time to spread.

questions.q: Who first adopted Robert Plath's improved wheeled suitcase?
a: Flight attendants, who became its first followers
Business travelers on long-haul routes
Airport staff who moved baggage
Luggage stores in major cities
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Plath sold first to flight attendants before the wider public caught on.

questions.q: Who solved the problem of telling time at sea?
a: A carpenter who built clocks in his spare time
An astronomer working for the British navy
A ship captain with decades of experience
A mathematician at a royal academy
questions.why: Lesson 3 says John Harrison was an outsider to sailing, and his clock design won the prize.
